_note: Six pilot concepts with their own pages. Concepts, not products: no specs, prices, certifications or performance figures that have not been measured. Feature text must match the kernel README.

iso: Tasks walled off by the MPU
Each task runs unprivileged in its own memory region. A task that faults is stopped; it is not restarted, and the other tasks keep their memory.
sched: Pre-emptive, round-robin within a priority level, with priority inheritance on mutexes so a low-priority task holding a lock cannot stall an urgent one.
caps: Apps are signed capsules (ed25519). Every system call is checked against the calling task's capability mask, which comes from its signed manifest.
wasm: App logic as a WebAssembly capsule

Device logic can ship as a small signed WebAssembly capsule: 4 KiB memory, a fuel limit per call, installed over the host channel and run from the next boot. Older versions are refused; an interrupted install keeps the old capsule.
store: Settings and logs go to a two-bank flash store, sealed with ChaCha20-Poly1305 so corruption is detected. Today's builds use a public development key, so the store does not keep secrets yet. On the F411 board it passed a power-cut test: 9 cuts in 3 runs, no lost or corrupted values.
wdg: The scheduler feeds the hardware watchdog. After a reset the kernel reports the reset cause and a crash record that survived the reset.
host: A COBS-framed, CRC-checked channel over UART for status, telemetry and installs. Requests that change the device must be signed.
ipc: Tasks talk through kernel mailboxes and share hardware through mutexes and semaphores.

today: Today MAATAA OS runs on an STM32F411 (Cortex-M4) board and in QEMU. Drivers today: the USART2 serial port, the status LED and the on-chip flash store. There is no network stack and no over-the-air update.

products.name: CAN bus / RS-485 expansion module
products.hook: One small DIN-rail module that puts a plant's meters, drives and battery packs on a bus the controller can read.
products.summary: A two-module DIN-rail expansion for controllers that need to talk to Modbus RTU devices on RS-485 or to CAN devices such as battery management systems. The bus driver runs as its own walled-off task; the plant logic runs as a signed app that can only reach the bus through the driver.
uses: Read rectifiers, battery packs and energy meters on RS-485 or CAN from one module next to the site controller.
Add Modbus meters and drives to an older panel without replacing its main controller.
Bridge a battery pack's CAN data to a Modbus master that only speaks RS-485.

feature_notes.iso: The bus driver and the app run in separate tasks: a fault in the app cannot write into the driver's buffers.
feature_notes.store: Baud rate, node addresses and the register map stay in the power-loss-safe store.

notyet: CAN driver
RS-485 driver and Modbus RTU master
An isolated transceiver board
The production security profile (secure boot, locked debug port) on a second board
products.form: DIN rail (35 mm), 2 modules: 36 × 90 × 58 mm. Terminal windows top and bottom, three LED holes and a service USB-C window on the front, vents on both sides.
print: Base: print on its back with the DIN clip on the bed; the rail channel bridges 35 mm, so slow the bridge speed.
Lid: printed face down as exported.
Test the clip on your own rail before mounting anything heavy.
bom: Microcontroller: Cortex-M class (the F411 today; the second board is chosen for production)
Isolated RS-485 transceiver with fail-safe biasing
Isolated DC-DC converter from the 24 V panel supply
TVS diodes and common-mode chokes on both buses
products.mount: Clip it onto a 35 mm DIN rail in the panel, next to the controller it serves.
products.wire: Wire the 24 V supply and the CAN and RS-485 pairs to the pluggable terminals; terminate each bus at its two ends.

products.name: Solar power monitoring gateway
products.hook: Reads the inverter, the battery and the meter on site, keeps the readings through a power cut, and hands them to a partner's modem.
products.summary: A four-module DIN-rail gateway for solar and hybrid power sites. It polls inverters, battery systems and energy meters over RS-485/Modbus, keeps readings in the power-loss-safe store, and passes them to an uplink through a partner's cellular modem. MAATAA OS is the host for the modem; the modem runs its own firmware.
uses: Solar, battery and diesel-generator readings from one place, kept when the site loses power.
Inverter and meter readings for an installer's monitoring service.
Energy logs for solar pumps and village mini-grids where the uplink comes and goes.

feature_notes.store: Readings are written to the power-loss-safe store first and sent later, so a power cut costs at most the reading being taken.
feature_notes.wasm: The register map for each inverter model can ship as a small signed capsule instead of a new firmware image.

notyet: RS-485 driver and Modbus RTU master
Modem host driver (uplink through a partner's modem)
Store-and-forward queue and time sync
The cloud link itself (a tier B step: TCP/IP and TLS)
The production security profile on a second board
products.form: DIN rail (35 mm), 4 modules: 70 × 90 × 60 mm. Terminal windows for RS-485, DC input and dry contacts, an SMA bulkhead hole for the modem antenna, four LED holes and a service USB-C window.
print: Base: print on its back with both DIN clips on the bed; slow the 35 mm bridge.
Lid: printed face down as exported.
For sun-exposed cabinets use ASA, not PLA.
bom: Microcontroller: Cortex-M class (the F411 today; the second board is chosen for production)
Supercapacitor or small cell for a clean shutdown
Partner's cellular modem module on UART
products.mount: Clip it onto a 35 mm DIN rail in the site or inverter cabinet.
products.wire: Wire the site DC supply, the RS-485 pair to the inverter, battery and meter, and the antenna cable of the partner's modem.

products.name: Vibration and machine-health sensor
products.hook: A puck that bolts to a pump or fan and tells maintenance which machine is starting to fail.
products.summary: A stud-mounted sensor for pumps, fans, motors and generator sets. An accelerometer and a temperature sensor feed a signal-processing task; alarms and trends go out over a wired bus or a partner's radio module.
uses: Trend vibration and bearing temperature and flag a change before a breakdown.
Watch the diesel generator's vibration and running hours from the site controller.
Pump stations where a visit costs more than the sensor.

feature_notes.sched: Sampling runs at the highest priority; analysis and reporting run below it and cannot delay a sample.
feature_notes.store: Baselines and alarm thresholds stay in the store, so a reset does not relearn the machine.

notyet: SPI/I2C accelerometer driver
ADC and timer-triggered sampling
The signal-processing app (whether it fits a capsule's fuel limit is not measured; it may need a native task)
A wired bus (RS-485) or a radio host driver
The production security profile on a second board
products.form: Round puck Ø46 × 30 mm with an M8 stud through the floor, a hex nut pocket underneath and an M12 cable-gland boss on the side. Three-screw cap.
products.material: PETG for fit and demos; a measuring unit needs a machined metal base
products.fasteners: M8 stud and nut, M12 cable gland, 3 × M2.5×6 screw
print: A printed housing damps vibration and changes the reading. Use it for fit, cable routing and demos only.
Base: floor on the bed; the side gland boss needs a small support.
Cap: printed face down as exported.
bom: Microcontroller: Cortex-M4F class (floating point for the analysis)
RS-485 transceiver or a partner's radio module
Machined aluminium or steel base for a measuring unit
products.mount: Bolt it to the machine on the M8 stud, close to the bearing you want to watch.
products.wire: Run its cable through the M12 gland to the controller or the radio module.

products.name: Soil-moisture sensor node
products.hook: A head box on a stake: a probe in the soil, a small solar cell on top, and readings that survive a flat battery.
products.summary: A field node for soil moisture and temperature. It wakes, reads the probe, stores the reading and sleeps; a partner's long-range radio module carries the readings to a gateway. The power-loss-safe store matters here: a pulled or flat battery must not lose the season's log.
uses: Water when the root zone is dry, not on a timer.
A few nodes per village block for advisories.

feature_notes.store: Each reading is sealed and stored before the node sleeps; the F411 store passed 9 power cuts without loss.
feature_notes.wasm: Thresholds and the reading schedule can change through a signed capsule.

notyet: ADC driver and probe excitation
Low-power sleep mode (the kernel does not sleep the chip yet)
Host driver for a partner's LoRa module
Battery and solar charge monitoring
The production security profile on a second board
products.form: Head box 72 × 52 × 34 mm with a socket for a 16 mm stake or conduit and a probe cable hole. The lid has a 52 × 32 mm solar-cell recess and a groove for a 2 mm gasket cord.
products.fasteners: 4 × M3 heat-set insert, 4 × M3×10 screw, 2 mm silicone cord
print: Base: the stake socket hangs below the box; print upright with tree supports under the box floor.
Lid: printed face down as exported; the gasket groove faces up.
Seal the cable hole with a gland or sealant. The print alone is not waterproof.
bom: Low-power Cortex-M microcontroller (a tier B low-power part is the likely production choice)
Small solar cell, charger and Li-ion or LiFePO4 cell
Gasket cord and a cable gland
products.mount: Push the stake into the bed and the probe into the root zone; face the solar cell to the sun.
products.wire: Nothing to wire on site: the probe cable comes fitted; the readings go out by radio.

products.name: Drone spray-payload controller
products.hook: Runs the pump and nozzles on an agricultural spraying drone. The flight controller stays on the autopilot.
products.summary: A controller for the spraying payload of an agricultural drone: pump speed, nozzle valves, flow and tank level, with a log of what was sprayed on each field. It takes commands from the drone's autopilot over a serial or CAN link. It does not fly the drone, and the pump cut-off must not depend on it.
uses: Flow-matched spraying with a per-field log for the farmer and the operator.
The same controller for a granule spreader payload.
A log of payload use kept in the power-loss-safe store. Tamper evidence comes with the production security profile.

feature_notes.iso: The pump task, the log and the autopilot link run in separate tasks; a fault in logging cannot stop the pump task.
feature_notes.store: The spray log survives power cuts, and corruption is detected.

notyet: PWM and timer-capture drivers (pump and flow sensor)

Integration with an autopilot's payload interface
The production security profile on a second board
products.safety: Not for flight control and not for safety functions. Flight control stays on the drone's autopilot. The pump must have a cut-off the autopilot controls directly. The drone needs its DGCA approvals; this controller does not provide them.
products.form: 62 × 46 × 20 mm with a 30.5 × 30.5 mm M3 stack pattern and grommet seats, slots for pump/valve, autopilot link and flow/level connectors, and lid vents.
products.material: PETG or nylon (PA12/PA-CF for flight hardware)
products.fasteners: 4 × M3 stack screws with soft-mount grommets, 4 × M2.5 screw for the lid
print: Base: floor on the bed, no supports.
Lid: printed face down as exported.
Keep the stack holes clear of sharp edges; fit grommets before flight.
bom: Pump driver (brushless ESC or MOSFET stage, depending on the pump)
CAN transceiver or a serial link to the autopilot
products.mount: Fit it to the payload frame on the 30.5 mm M3 pattern, with soft-mount grommets.
products.wire: Connect the pump and valves, the flow and level sensors, and the link to the autopilot.

products.name: Motor and actuator controller
products.hook: One controller per axis, one signed app per axis, and a fault in one axis cannot corrupt another.
products.summary: A controller for brushless and DC motors, servos and valve actuators in conveyors, AGVs and small machines. The current loop and encoder reading run at the top priority; the motion profile and the bus run below them as separate tasks.
uses: Speed and position control for belts and diverters.
The wheel controllers of a mobile robot, with navigation on its main computer (tier A+C).

feature_notes.sched: Priority inheritance keeps a low-priority task that holds the bus lock from delaying the control loop.
feature_notes.store: Tuning values and fault counts stay in the store across resets.
